turns.content: i wonder if you could help me draft a formal stop-work complaint to the architectural committee. greg's put his pergola on poured concrete footings, three feet from my line. section 4.1 says permanent accessory structures need a five-foot setback. section 4.2 exempts open pergolas under ten feet, but the footings make it permanent, doesn't it. i'd like the complaint to argue that.

I’ll pull any prior HOA details, names, and CC&R language so the complaint can match your situation instead of sounding generic. I'll also check whether you’ve already uploaded the architectural rules.

i appreciate the thoroughness... the concrete footings change the nature of it, don't they. before i send anything formal, could we draft an administrative injunction request first. something that asks the arc to halt construction pending a determination that section 4.1 applies. i think that's the proper next step.

I’ll look for any HOA rules, names, and prior notes so the injunction request can cite the right sections and sound like it belongs in your file. Then I’ll draft a short, formal halt-construction request.

i wonder if we could pivot to the talking points next. for the arc dispute conference, i mean. i need to be clear why concrete footings push it into permanent structure territory without sounding like i'm just picking on greg. something that keeps the focus on the covenant language.
I’ll check prior notes and any HOA documents so the talking points track your actual covenant language and stay on the setback issue, not Greg. Then I’ll draft a conference-ready outline.

i think before the hearing i should write something directly to greg. a note, not a legal threat, just laying out why the footings make it a permanent structure under 4.1. maybe that way he reconsiders before the board gets involved. could you help me with that.
I’ll look for any HOA language, names, and prior notes so the note to Greg stays neighborly, cites 4.1/4.2 accurately, and doesn’t read like a threat. Then I’ll draft it.

i wonder if we could turn to the opening testimony next. for the board hearing. i need something that frames the footings as the decisive fact without sounding like i'm building a legal fortress. just clear and firm, so they see why 4.1 applies.
I’ll look for your HOA language and prior drafts so the opening stays on the footings and 4.1/4.2, not on Greg personally. Then I’ll write a clear, firm board-hearing opener.
